cards.text: Gideon, also called Jerubbaal, has died, and Israel has set up Baal-berith as their god (Judges 8:32-33, 35). His son Abimelech was born to Gideon's concubine in Shechem (Judges 8:31). Now Abimelech goes to Shechem, to his mother's brothers and his mother's whole clan.
Gideon had SEVENTY sons (Judges 8:30). Friend, I've got six little ones and I ran out of stations to name. Now Abimelech wants his uncles to carry a question to all the leaders of Shechem.

cards.question: What question does Abimelech want his uncles to put to the leaders of Shechem?

answers.text: Is seventy men ruling better than one
Is Baal better than the LORD
Is peace better than fighting Midian

cards.text: The uncles bring the pitch to all the leaders of Shechem, and the leaders' hearts lean toward Abimelech. Friend, I know how a good pitch gets you. A guy once sold me an oven timer that SINGS, and I bought three.

cards.question: What reason do the leaders of Shechem give for following Abimelech?
The leaders of Shechem give Abimelech seventy shekels of silver from the temple of ___.
Abimelech uses the silver to hire worthless and reckless men to follow him.

cards.text: Then Abimelech goes to his father's house in Ophrah. There, he murders his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal.

cards.question: Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, survives. How?

answers.text: He was out in the fields

cards.text: Then all the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo gather beside the oak at the pillar in Shechem.

cards.question: Beside the oak at the pillar, the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo make Abimelech their ___.

cards.text: Gideon once told Israel, "I will not rule over you, nor will my son." (Judges 8:23) Well, friend, one of his sons just took the job anyway.
Somebody reports all of this to Jotham, the youngest brother, the one who hid.

cards.question: Where does Jotham go to speak to the leaders of Shechem?

cards.text: He raises his voice: "Listen to me, O leaders of Shechem, and may God listen to you." Then he tells them a story: one day the trees set out to anoint a king for themselves.

cards.question: In Jotham's story, the trees ask the olive tree to reign over them first. What does the olive tree say?

answers.text: It won't stop giving its oil to rule
It will rule if all trees obey it
It needs time to think it over

cards.text: I bet the olive tree likes its job too much to trade it for sitting in meetings all day. Next, the trees ask the fig tree to come and reign over them.

cards.question: In Jotham's story, the fig tree agrees to reign over the trees.

cards.text: The fig tree won't give up its sweetness and its good fruit either, so the trees try the grapevine. Third interview, friend, and NOBODY wants the corner office.

cards.question: In Jotham's story, the grapevine won't stop giving its ___ that cheers both God and man.

cards.text: Finally, all the trees go to the thornbush and ask it to come and reign over them. The THORNBUSH, friend, the one plant everybody walks around.

cards.question: In Jotham's story, the thornbush answers with an if. If the trees really are anointing it king, what does it tell them to do?

cards.text: And if not, the thornbush says, may fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon. Friend, that's the worst job interview I've ever heard: hire me, or I burn the place down.

Then Jotham turns to the leaders and starts with an if: if they have acted faithfully and honestly in making Abimelech king. For his father fought for them and risked his life to deliver them from the hand of Midian.

cards.question: Jotham tells the leaders of Shechem they have killed his father's seventy sons on a single ___.
Jotham says the leaders made Abimelech, the son of his father's maidservant, king because he is their brother.
If the leaders of Shechem have acted faithfully and honestly toward Jerubbaal's house, what does Jotham say may happen?

answers.text: Rejoice in Abimelech and he in them
Have rest in their land again
Be blessed with a good harvest

cards.question: But if not, Jotham says, may ___ come from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and come from the leaders and consume Abimelech.

cards.text: Jotham has said his piece to the leaders of Shechem, and then he RUNS. Friend, that's exactly how I'd handle a hard conversation too.

cards.question: Where does Jotham escape to and live after his message to the leaders of Shechem?
Jotham settles down to live in Beer. Why does he stay there?

answers.text: He wants to raise an army

cards.text: Keep that apron tied, friend, because this story isn't finished.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the fact about Gideon's sons, Papa Dorin's joke, and the setup about Abimelech's question.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks for a detail the baker cannot reason out. The earlier cards omitted the one stone from Judges 9:5, and nothing in the setup distinguishes stone from altar or hill, so the baker can only guess.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
